solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Where they serve drinks attractive to weightwatchers?

explanation.surface: A wry question about which bar would appeal to people on a diet.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two pieces, LO CAL, the advertising shorthand for low-calorie food and drink, and it suits a dieter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a person's nearest pub is called their local, the place that serves them drinks.

clue.text: Bird rescue vessel is checking one waiting on air

indicators.note: something on air is broadcast, so we want the sound of these words rather than their spelling

parts.note: Noah's ark rescued the animals from the Flood
checking items off a list is ticking them; tick's is a contraction of tick is
someone standing in a queue is a queuer

explanation.surface: A bird spotted near a rescue ship, apparently being checked over while it waits for broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'ark tick's queuer' is how the bird's name is pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic skua is a gull-like seabird that breeds in northern regions and chases other birds for food.

clue.text: Made money in boarding school

indicators.note: a boarder lodges inside a school, so one word is taken to live inside the other

parts.note: a coed is a coeducational school, for boys and girls together
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who earned a fortune while at boarding school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In boarding school' reads as one phrase; the word in is the passenger that boards the school.
explanation.definitionFit: To coin is literally to stamp metal into currency, so coined is made money.

clue.text: Every second in Buckingham Palace stirring, but husband's missing a volcano

indicators.note: stirring mixes things around, so the gathered letters are rearranged
the husband is missing, so his letter is dropped from the collection
every second letter means taking the even-numbered letters of the following words

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on
H is the standard abbreviation for husband
taken as written, added at the end

explanation.surface: Things stirring at Buckingham Palace while a husband has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of Buckingham Palace include an H; drop it, rearrange the other seven and finish with A.
explanation.definitionFit: Mauna Kea is a dormant volcano on Hawaii's Big Island, famous for its summit observatories.

clue.text: Person who helped produce Poliakoff's persona stays on at Reading?

indicators.note: stays hold something up and enclose it, like a corset, so one piece holds the others

parts.note: Nicolai Poliakoff performed as Coco the Clown
re means on or about, as in a letter heading
taken as written
reading is one of the three Rs

explanation.surface: A question about a character played by someone called Poliakoff staying on at Reading, the English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Poliakoff suggests the dramatist Stephen, but here it is Nicolai, the circus clown Coco, whose name wraps round the next two words before R is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-creator is one of two or more people who jointly made a work.

clue.text: Argentinian leader admitting to war could somehow discourage

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters come out in a new arrangement
to admit is to let in, so the leader's name lets the other letters inside

parts.note: Juan Peron was president of Argentina
these letters plus the word could, rearranged

explanation.surface: Argentina's president confesses to a war, which might deter others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Argentinian leader' tempts you to take just A; it is Peron, who splits after P to take in the shuffled 'to war could'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pour cold water on an idea is an idiom for being negative about it and dampening enthusiasm.

clue.text: Dedicate time to V-E Day whirling displays

indicators.note: whirling turns things round, so the letters are read the other way
to display is to show, so the answer is on show within the words

parts.note: found across the end of time, all of to and the start of V-E Day

explanation.surface: Spending time on spinning celebrations for Victory in Europe Day.
explanation.definitionFit: To devote time or effort to something is to dedicate it to that purpose.

clue.text: Say 'Go', but not love drive

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as say does

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so the named letter is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Telling someone to go without affection, as one might urge them on.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone, usually egg on, is to urge or push them forward.

clue.text: Chip vans — aren't I glad they're here!

definitions.text: Chip vans — aren't I glad they're here!

indicators.note: to chip is to break into pieces, so the letters that follow are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: all fourteen letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A happy customer greeting the arrival of fish-and-chip vans.
explanation.walkthrough: Chip looks like part of a compound noun; it is the anagram signal, and the whole exclamation also describes the seasonings, glad to be on the chips.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt and vinegar are the classic British seasonings shaken over chips, there wherever chips are sold.

clue.text: A blast from the past, online order from …

parts.note: E stands for electronic, as in e-mail
COD is cash on delivery, a way of paying for goods ordered

explanation.surface: Something nostalgic, perhaps an internet order from a takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into the next clue, so the order seems to be a fish from a takeaway; it is cash on delivery, and the answer is an old-fashioned oath.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecod is an archaic mild exclamation like egad, so it is literally an outburst from former times.

clue.text: …less thematic establishment?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a shop selling ready meals, here the fish and chip shop at the heart of this puzzle's theme

explanation.walkthrough: 'Thematic' points to the puzzle's fish-and-chips theme; 'less' is the arithmetic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic 'take away' is the spoken minus, and a takeaway is also a shop selling food to eat elsewhere.

clue.text: Better Samuel's teacher or a friend on tour?

indicators.note: a band on tour moves around from place to place, so these letters move around too

parts.note: in the Bible the priest Eli raised the boy Samuel
taken as written
taken as written
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: Asking whether a teacher or a travelling friend would be the better choice.
explanation.walkthrough: Better is a verb here, not a comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To ameliorate a situation is to improve it, and to better something is the same.

clue.text: Time zone crossed by fresh Chinese thinker

indicators.note: the outer word is crossed by, so has running through it, the other letters
fresh means new, so the word is given a new form

parts.note: the seven letters rearranged
T is the abbreviation for time
Z is the abbreviation for zone

explanation.surface: A new Chinese philosopher who straddles a time zone.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Nietzsche was a nineteenth-century German philosopher, an example of a thinker.

clue.text: Brahms and Liszt behind the elite?

parts.note: the pick of the bunch is its best members
followers come behind, so they are led

explanation.surface: A question about two famous composers trailing behind the top performers.
explanation.walkthrough: Brahms and Liszt is Cockney rhyming slang for pissed, meaning drunk. Being behind the elite is being led by the pick: the clue words are reversed in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickled is informal for very drunk, the meaning the rhyming slang stands for.

clue.text: Essex duo engineering more than one way out

indicators.note: engineering means building or contriving, so the letters are worked into a new structure

parts.note: the eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A pair from Essex, an English county, planning a series of escapes.
explanation.definitionFit: An exodus is a mass departure, so the plural gives several ways out.

clue.text: Perhaps love is aroused inside banger

indicators.note: inside places the stirred letters within the other word
being aroused means being stirred up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the four letters rearranged
say means perhaps, as in say ten

explanation.surface: Romance awakening inside a sausage, absurdly.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A saveloy is a highly seasoned red sausage sold in chip shops, so a kind of banger.

clue.text: One's cold, with age wearing away — and picking up speed

definitions.text: One's cold, with age wearing away — and picking up speed

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: something wearing away is gradually lost, so those letters disappear from the word

parts.note: taken as written
with age means old

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up means lifting from bottom to top, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: pace is rate of movement

explanation.surface: Something frozen that is eroding over time, and faster and faster.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's just joins one to cold. With age means old, which wears away from cold to leave its first letter; the whole clue pictures polar ice melting at an accelerating rate.
explanation.definitionFit: A polar ice cap is a cold mass that is shrinking over the years at a growing rate.

clue.text: Alien about to be received by Vietnam Police compound …

indicators.note: something received is taken in, so these letters go inside the following pair

parts.note: E.T. is the alien of Spielberg's film
Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam, standing for the country's government
ca is short for circa, about
the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial about to be taken in by the Vietnamese police.
explanation.walkthrough: Vietnam Police reads as one body; the about-word sits between the capital and the detectives.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethanoic acid is the systematic name for acetic acid, the chemical compound in vinegar.

clue.text: See 18
Surgically remove tip of biceps muscle in A&E

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the next pair

parts.note: taken letter for letter
the lats, latissimus dorsi, are back muscles

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its very first letter

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A doctor in Accident and Emergency removing the end of an arm muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is Britain's accident and emergency hospital department, but here only its letters are wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To ablate tissue is the surgical term for cutting it away or destroying it.

clue.text: With cushions, piano lifted on top

indicators.note: something lifted is taken away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: with cushions means padded
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Movers raise a piano onto something cushioned.
explanation.walkthrough: The piano is not a musical instrument being hoisted; it is the letter removed from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on top is in addition, extra, and so added.

clue.text: … another one briefly taken in manacles

parts.words: another one briefly taken in manacles
parts.note: surface reading: one more prisoner handcuffed for a short while
setter's reading: the compound in its brief form, its chemical formula, sits in the middle of manacles

explanation.surface: A further prisoner put in handcuffs for a short time.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues from the previous compound clue. 'Briefly' asks for the short form of the compound, its formula NaCl, which hides inside manacles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium chloride, common salt, is another chemical compound, following on from the previous clue's acid.

clue.text: Mayo? Chilli sauce? Not much 20 to haddock, in essence

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so the central letter of the word is kept

parts.note: its central letter, fourth of seven
1p, a single penny, is not much money; read as letters

explanation.surface: A chip-shop question: which sauce to put on the haddock, though only a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 stands for the answer to 20 down, so read 'not much added to'; the 1 of 1p doubles as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayonnaise and chilli sauce are both dips, sauces you dunk food into.

clue.text: Tate has brown tube?

parts.note: surface reading: the London gallery owning a brown pipe
setter's reading: tater, hash brown and tuber, each a potato, each with its last letter chipped off

explanation.surface: The Tate gallery acquiring a brown tube, perhaps as modern art.
explanation.walkthrough: Tater is slang for a potato, a hash brown is a fried potato cake and a tuber is what a potato is; clip the final letter of each and you get the clue's words.
explanation.definitionFit: Every word in the clue is a potato that has been chipped, trimmed at the end, which is the punning sense of the phrase.
